content: The Tao is like a great river that flows everywhere. It is the Mother of the world.
author: Lao Tzu
sourceWork: Tao Te Ching, Book of Virtue
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Most human unhappiness exists in two places that don't currently exist: the past, which cannot be changed, and the future, which hasn't happened yet. Meanwhile, the only life you will ever experience is slipping past unnoticed.

In Lao Tzu's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Presence is not a rare mystical achievement; it is simply having the courtesy to show up for your own life. When you anchor your awareness in the immediate room and task, the frantic anxieties of the ego dissolve.
reflectionPrompt: How can you create a moment of stillness today to reconnect with your deeper sense of purpose?
